metadata.name: routerpulse
metadata.description: DePIN Wi-Fi uptime tracking protocol on Solana

accounts.name: vesting
docs: `init` (not `init_if_needed`): one vesting record per epoch,
ever. Combined with the `claimed` flag on the epoch, this makes
double-claiming fail two independent ways.

accounts.name: cranker
docs: Whoever is turning the crank. Pays rent for the epoch's emission
account if they happen to be the first to finalize it; otherwise
only the transaction fee. Deliberately not required to be the
operator or the authority.

accounts.name: device
docs: The device key registered for this router — NOT the owner
wallet. See `rotate_device_key` for recovery from a compromised
device.

accounts.name: reward_mint
docs: Reward mint, created here as a PDA with the protocol PDA as its
sole mint authority. No freeze authority is set: the protocol
can issue and slash, but must not be able to freeze a holder's
tokens.

accounts.name: stake_vault
docs: Holds every operator's staked collateral.

accounts.name: treasury
docs: Receives slashed collateral.

types.name: EmissionSchedule
docs: Per-epoch emission budget — the hard cap on how many reward tokens
that epoch can ever mint.
Created lazily on the first `finalize_router_epoch` for an epoch and
debited by each router's reward as it finalizes. Without this, reward
issuance would be unbounded: `reward_rate * epoch_duration * routers`
grows with the router count, so a Sybil operator registering many
routers could inflate supply arbitrarily. Here, extra routers dilute
a fixed pool instead of expanding it.

fields.name: total_emission
docs: Budget for this epoch, snapshotted at creation from the
protocol's decaying emission curve.

fields.name: allocated
docs: Sum of all rewards finalized against this epoch so far.

fields.name: authority
docs: The admin who can update protocol settings

fields.name: reward_rate
docs: Reward tokens earned per second of uptime per router

fields.name: epoch_duration
docs: Length of one reward epoch, in seconds. Rewards are only ever
paid out for a *closed* epoch, computed from heartbeats actually
received inside that epoch's time window — never from a lifetime
counter that can go stale while a router is silently offline.

fields.name: genesis_time
docs: Unix timestamp the protocol was initialized. Epoch numbers are
derived deterministically from this, so no cross-router cranking
is ever required to "advance" the epoch clock.

fields.name: reward_mint
docs: SPL mint for the reward token. Mint authority is the protocol
PDA itself, so issuance is only ever possible through this
program's instructions — never by a human holding a key.

fields.name: min_stake
docs: Collateral a router must have staked before it may heartbeat or
earn. This is what gives slashing teeth.

fields.name: stake_lock_duration
docs: How long staked collateral is locked after each `stake` call.

fields.name: reward_cliff_duration
docs: Cliff/duration applied to every epoch reward entitlement.

fields.name: initial_emission_per_epoch
docs: Per-epoch emission budget before decay, and the decay curve.

fields.name: genesis_allocation
docs: Hard cap on the initial distribution. Rewards can only be minted
by vesting, and staking requires already holding tokens — so
without a genesis allocation no operator could ever bootstrap.
Fixed at initialization and enforced on-chain, so the authority
can distribute up to this much and then never mint again.

types.name: RewardVesting
docs: One epoch's reward entitlement, released on a cliff + linear
schedule.
No tokens are moved when this is created — it records only the
right to mint. `claim_vested` mints the newly-vested slice straight
to the operator, so supply grows exactly in step with what has
actually vested and there is no vault balance to drift out of sync
or be drained.

fields.name: total_amount
docs: Full entitlement for the epoch. `claimed` can never exceed it.

fields.name: cliff_duration
docs: Nothing vests before `start_time + cliff_duration`.

fields.name: vesting_duration
docs: Fully vested at `start_time + vesting_duration`.

fields.name: owner
docs: The wallet that owns and operates this router.
Responsible for paying penalties and receiving rewards.
This is NOT the key that signs heartbeats — see `device_pubkey`.

fields.name: device_pubkey
docs: The key that signs heartbeat transactions on behalf of the
physical device. Separated from `owner` so the operator's main
wallet is never exposed to an unattended router, and so a
compromised device can be recovered via `rotate_device_key`
without re-registering the router.

fields.name: device_key_version
docs: Incremented every time the device key is rotated. Lets an
indexer / audit trail distinguish "old device, new device"
heartbeats after a recovery event.

fields.name: router_id
docs: Unique hardware identifier , max 32 characters
Example: "router-mumbai-001" or device MAC hash

fields.name: location_lat
docs: GPS coordinates as fixed-point integers
Multiply actual coordinate by 1_000_000
Avoids floating point (not supported in Solana BPF)

fields.name: registered_at
docs: Unix timestamp when router was registered

fields.name: last_heartbeat
docs: Unix timestamp of most recent heartbeat

fields.name: uptime_score
docs: Real-time uptime score 0–100, used only for fast suspension
response. This is a complementary signal to the per-epoch
reward accounting in `RouterEpoch` — it reacts immediately to
bad behaviour but is never itself used to compute a payout.

fields.name: total_rewards
docs: Lifetime earnings in token units

fields.name: total_penalties
docs: Lifetime penalties deducted

fields.name: heartbeat_count
docs: Total heartbeats received

fields.name: missed_heartbeats
docs: Total heartbeats missed or late

fields.name: staked_amount
docs: Mirror of the router's `Stake.amount`, denormalized onto the
router so `heartbeat` can enforce the minimum-stake gate without
loading a second account on every single check-in. Kept in sync
by stake / unstake / slash — those are the only writers.

fields.name: status
docs: Current operational status of this router

fields.name: bump
docs: Canonical PDA bump — stored during registration

types.name: RouterEpoch
docs: Per-router, per-epoch performance record. Created lazily on a
router's first heartbeat inside a given epoch, closed by
`finalize_router_epoch` once the epoch's time window has elapsed,
and consumed exactly once by `claim_reward`.
This account — not the lifetime counters on `Router` — is the
source of truth for rewards. A router that goes silent simply never
accumulates a `RouterEpoch` for the epochs it missed, so it cannot
coast on a stale historical uptime percentage the way a
claim-from-lifetime-average design would allow.

fields.name: heartbeats
docs: Heartbeats actually received inside [start_time, end_time).

fields.name: expected_heartbeats
docs: ceil(epoch_duration / heartbeat_interval) at the time this
epoch record was opened — the denominator for uptime_bps.

fields.name: finalized
docs: Set once by `finalize_router_epoch`, after which `heartbeats`
is frozen and a reward amount is locked in.

fields.name: claimed
docs: Set once by `claim_reward`. Prevents double-claiming the same
epoch.

fields.name: uptime_bps
docs: Uptime for this epoch in basis points (0-10_000), fixed at
finalization time.

fields.name: reward_amount
docs: Reward token amount locked in at finalization, granted verbatim
on claim. Already has the performance-tier multiplier applied
and is capped by the epoch's remaining emission budget.

fields.name: slash_amount
docs: Collateral to slash for this epoch's performance, fixed at
finalization from the same tier table as the reward.

fields.name: slashed
docs: Set once by `slash_router`, so one bad epoch can only ever be
slashed a single time.

types.name: Stake
docs: Per-router stake position. Collateral an operator must post before a
router can earn: it is what makes slashing meaningful, since a
router with nothing at risk can spam bad uptime for free.
The tokens themselves live in one shared protocol-owned stake vault;
this account is the per-router accounting record against it.

fields.name: amount
docs: Currently staked, net of anything already slashed.

fields.name: total_slashed
docs: Lifetime total slashed away from this position.

fields.name: locked_until
docs: Unstaking is blocked until this timestamp. Set forward on every
new stake so collateral can't be posted to pass an activation
check and then yanked out in the same epoch.
